s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with radiation to the jaw and associated symptoms
salient_findings: Chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression on ECG
key_facts: Subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, dry cough, and sinus congestion 4 days prior to presentation
3 hours of substernal pressure that resolved spontaneously the day prior to presentation
Constant chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
Initial serum troponin I level of 6.18 ng/mL
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin and inflammatory markers with normal coronary arteries

shortlist.label: Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain with radiation to the jaw, elevated inflammatory markers, and PR-segment depression on ECG

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin level, although coronary angiography showed normal coronary arteries

shortlist.label: Acute coronary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pressure and elevated troponin, although coronary arteries are normal

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain with radiation to the jaw, elevated troponin, and normal coronary arteries, with potential stress trigger

trace.fact: Chest pressure radiating to the right jaw

rule_in.why: it is a classic symptom of myocardial infarction

rule_out.why: radiation to jaw is possible in all candidates

rule_in.why: it is commonly associated with diaphoresis

rule_out.why: diaphoresis is compatible with all candidates

rule_in.why: it is most closely associated with elevated serum troponin I level

rule_out.why: it is less commonly associated with elevated troponin I levels
